gaps.fact: Santorini warm Mediterranean and Naoussa continental: only the two articles name the categories; the chapter says only that Santorini has almost no rain, and no question asks either climate.
Sigalas, the Court's one Greek name: it stands in the santorini article only; no chapter names it and no question asks it.

Santorini Assyrtiko with seafood, roasted fish and fresh cheeses, and Naoussa Xinomavro, often oak aged, with lamb and beef whose fat tames its tannin: the articles carry both, but no question in either bank pairs a Greek wine with food.

notes: Mapped questions: Village 41 (Hungary & Greece, of which 19 are Greek and 22 Hungarian), Régionale 0 (a Certified only subject; the two Greek Régionale stems are listed in the coverage), 41 in all. The Court's three PDOs are well taught: Santorini's Assyrtiko on ash and pumice, the kouloura, ungrafted vines renewed by layering, Nykteri and Vinsanto; Naoussa as Xinomavro alone on Mount Vermio with the Nebbiolo comparison; Nemea as Agiorgitiko alone; and beyond the Court, Amyndeon, Goumenissa, Rapsani, Mantinia, Retsina, Cava and the PGI tier. The thin cells are the two climate categories, Sigalas and Greek wine at the table; the Court's two seas are named together only in the country article (i-uqmxmmsn places Santorini in the Aegean, and the Ionian Sea is never asked). No factual error found: Santorini white at 85 per cent Assyrtiko with Athiri and Aidani (the article rightly notes the older 75 per cent rule, raised by an amendment published in 2022, before the guide), Nykteri at 13.5 per cent and three months in oak, Vinsanto with two years in oak, Naoussa red only and unblended, Rapsani in equal thirds and Goumenissa with Negoska all hold. Two searches spent, on the Santorini, Naoussa and Nemea specifications: the only amendment found (the Assyrtiko share, 2022) predates the guide, and no change since 8.2023 was found, so courtUpdates is empty.
